issue_title: Keep the operator loop moving overnight
issue_body: Plan approvals and infrastructure retries stall from evening until someone is back at the keyboard. Let a repository run the operator role on a schedule, inside the workflow's delegation knobs, and record which instance acted on each gate.

plan.summary: Add an optional schedule block to the operator role spec and a cron-driven instance of the role that approves and retries within the workflow's operator_agent knobs.

approach.description: Add an optional schedule block (a cron expression and a knob preset name) to docs/spec/operator-role.schema.json, mirror it with scripts/sync-schemas, and decode it in operatorrole.go.

Add a scheduler harness in backend/internal/operatorrole/scheduler.go that, on each cron tick, instantiates the role from the shipped versioned playbook and drives approvals and retries under the existing operator-agent/<role-spec-version> token subject, since the role contract lets any harness, a scheduler included, instantiate the role.
Record every action the scheduled instance takes with the instance id and the cron tick that triggered it, and document the schedule block in the operatorrole package README.
Add tests: a tick inside the knobs approves a clean plan, a tick facing an undelegated gate pages instead, and a spec without a schedule block runs no instance.

verification.test_strategy: Unit tests over a fake clock and a fake gate store for each tick outcome, plus schema validation tests for a present and an absent schedule block.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR; the schedule block is optional and a spec without it runs nothing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every approval or retry the scheduled instance makes is recorded with the instance that acted and the tick that triggered it.
A gate the workflow's knobs do not delegate is paged to a human, never acted on by the scheduled instance.

defect_phrases: lets any harness, a scheduler included, instantiate the role
drives approvals and retries under the existing

catching_examples.note: Step 2 runs the role unattended under the operator-agent/<role-spec-version> subject because ADR-040 lets any harness instantiate it. ADR-040 is superseded by ADR-101: sustained unattended operation needs a captain-issued charter lease and a product-spawned operator holding only the per-lease credential. Route the scheduled instance through a charter lease, or needs an amending ADR.

The scheduler harness rests on ADR-040's any-harness model, which the index marks superseded by ADR-101; ADR-101 D5 runs unattended actions under a per-lease credential held by a product-spawned operator.
An instance acting under operator-agent/<role-spec-version> on a cron is not a charter session; unattended approvals now need a live lease.

non_catching_examples.note: Step 2: the choice of a cron trigger is unjustified.
Step 2 lets the scheduled instance approve plans; ADR-083 keeps the captain seat human, so confirm the instance never takes a captain verb.
The scheduler harness in step 2 follows ADR-040; cite it in the plan.
ac-scheduled-action-recorded does not say where the record is kept.
